takeaways: Anything that moves, blinks or scrolls on its own for more than 5 seconds, next to other content, needs a way to pause, stop or hide it.
Content that updates on its own, such as a live feed or ticker, needs a way to pause, stop or hide it, or to control how often it updates.
Movement pulls the eye away from what people are trying to read. For some people it makes the rest of the page unusable.
Motion that is essential to the activity is exempt. A decorative or promotional animation almost never is.
failures: An auto-advancing carousel with no pause button
A looping background video with no stop control
A news ticker or live score feed that cannot be paused
check: Open each screen and wait. List everything that moves or changes without you touching it.
For each item that runs longer than 5 seconds, find the visible pause, stop or hide control.
Check that the control works by keyboard, not only by hovering over the moving area.

quiz.question: A homepage hero carousel auto-advances every 6 seconds and loops forever. The team says it pauses on hover. Is that enough?
options: No. Add a visible pause button that keyboard and touch users can reach
Yes. Pausing on hover is a pause mechanism
Yes, because each slide shows for longer than 5 seconds
quiz.why: Hover does nothing for keyboard, touch or screen reader users, so they still cannot stop it. The 5 seconds is about how long the motion lasts overall, not each slide.

spec: List every element that moves or updates automatically, with how long it runs.
Draw the pause, stop or hide control for each, with its position, label and both states.
Note whether the paused state is remembered when people move between pages.
review: What on this screen moves without anyone asking it to?
Where is the pause button, and can you reach it without a mouse?
Does this animation need to loop at all?
tradeoff: Marketing wants motion to catch the eye, and that is exactly what makes it hard for others to read. Let it play once and stop, or keep it running with a clear pause control near the start of the component.
system: Give the carousel, video background and ticker components a built-in pause control that cannot be turned off.
pitch: If people cannot stop the carousel, many of them stop reading the page instead.
